answer: Standing decays sharply after 8 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. The bridge decay curve is applied at each close, pulse records the drop, and haven recomputes standing from replay. A farm that parks aliases between attacks thus finds them worthless when it returns to them. That bill is paid per identity, so 289 aliases cost 324 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
